cases.reviewerAnswer: In affirmative instructions, habla addresses tú, hablad addresses vosotros, hable addresses usted, and hablen addresses ustedes.
cases.element: content.body.variantPolicyUk: «двох адресатів (наприклад, usted і él/ella в оповіданні)»
cases.defect: A narrative él/ella identifies a third-person subject, not an alternative addressee. The policy conflates identifying an addressee with distinguishing directive and narrative readings.
cases.correction: Distinguish the subject of a narrative from the addressee of an instruction. Require enough context to establish a directive reading before assessing its addressee.
sources: RAE/ASALE, Nueva gramática de la lengua española, chapters 16 (personal pronouns and forms of address) and 42 (modality and imperative constructions) (from memory).
cases.notes: The four affirmative imperative forms themselves are correct.

cases.reviewerAnswer: avisar means «попереджати, повідомляти»; Avísame means «дай мені знати».
encender means «вмикати; запалювати»; its third-person singular present form is enciende.
girar means «повертати» in directions such as turning right or left.
mirar means «дивитися»; ¡Mira! can be translated as «Подивися!»
seguir means «продовжувати; іти далі»; Sigue hasta la plaza means «Іди далі до площі».
Regular affirmative tú forms include habla, come and escribe; the listed stem changes give cierra, vuelve and pide. Vosotros forms include hablad, comed and escribid.

cases.defect: The lesson states a blanket rule that vosotros imperative forms have no written accent. Bare forms such as oíd and reíd require one. The listed examples are correct, but the orthographic generalization is misleading.
cases.correction: Limit the statement to the forms taught here: «У наведених формах знак наголосу не потрібен: hablad, comed, escribid». Revise the summary accordingly.
